summary:
FIVE ITEMS FIXED, ONE ALREADY LANDED AND CONFIRMED, ONE CARRIER REFUTED, AND TWO THINGS FOUND BY DRIVING THAT NOBODY FILED.

ITEM 1 IS REAL AND WAS WORSE THAN FILED. cap.valve computed `vocab_room = vocab_armed and 0 < cv < hard_vocab` and never consulted the honesty precondition, so on CAP_TARGETS=vocab CAP_VOCAB_START=1000 LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS=0 it printed `Gate cap.valve: FIRED ... an armed arm has room to earn` while observe's closed set refuses EVERY lift that arm earns, by name, every flush. I drove all four CAP_TARGETS crossed with LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS 0/1 and confirmed the predecessor's eight-corner control is VACUOUS: on all eight, cap.valve is UNREACHABLE by construction (both starts are the sentinel, which resolves to the hard ceiling), so the control ran entirely inside the arm that is switched off and could not have detected anything. THEN I FOUND A FIFTH DEAD-ON-ARRIVAL NOBODY FILED, on CAP's own two levers with no wire involved: derive.lift_to(c, frac, floor) = c + max(int(floor), int(frac*c)) returns the cap UNCHANGED when both terms round to zero, so at CAP_TARGETS=experts CAP_FAB_START=12 CAP_LIFT_MIN=0 the valve can earn a lift forever and nothing moves -- and it printed FIRED. capacity/levers.py::CAPLevers already writes that exact case down as the reason lift_min exists ('at cap 12, int(0.08 x 12) = 0 ... the cap can never move again, on any evidence, forever ... reachable in the first place this rebuild runs'), so it is documented, reachable, and was unmeasured. Both terms are now in the predicate, in the printed arithmetic, and in the `dead` list.

THE FIX IS PROVED BY AN 80-ROW BEFORE/AFTER MATRIX against a pure-HEAD mirror (git archive HEAD, outside the repo). 13 of 80 rows changed and EVERY SINGLE ONE is FIRED -> UNREACHABLE: not one row gained a FIRED, so no configuration lost a capability -- only false FIREDs were removed. cap.vocab_arm_honest is byte-identical on all 80 rows, which is the non-vacuous version of the control D15 deserved and never got (80 rows, not 8).

ITEM 2 CONFIRMED EXACTLY. spine/assemble.py::NOT_WIRES holds SEVEN rows, enumerated by import, and neither d_curve_bpb nor d_shift_at is among them; both are rows 2 and 4 of docs/04_CONTRACT.md section 0's separate 12-row refused-candidates table. All three sites corrected. THE RULING SURVIVES INTACT AND DOES NOT DEPEND ON THE CITATION: the ground -- a Coupling.compute sees only frozen Configs -- is stated verbatim in the correct table's own preamble, is held down by tests/test_couplings.py's C2, and both candidates are refused on it for reasons the table gives (a held-out measurement; an optimizer step index). Only the place was wrong.

ITEM 3 CONFIRMED BY BUILDING THE RECORD: new_valve seeds EIGHT counters keys and the RECORD TYPES line named six. Fixed, with the count spelled and both omissions named.

ITEM 4 CONFIRMED AND THE CARRIER COUNT WAS ITSELF SHORT. Live: 23 declared couplings, 19 cross-package wires of WIRE_BUDGET=25, 4 intra-package -- SIX edges remain. I found FOUR carriers, not one. Two are mine and are fixed (src/capacity/levers.py, whose CONSEQUENCE clause was false too -- adding the four couplings it discusses takes the ledger 19 -> 23 of 25 and build() does not refuse it; and docs/04_CONTRACT.md's Q-WORLD-6 'one of the last lines'). Two are not mine and are filed under unfinished with exact find/replace text. ONE CANDIDATE I REFUTE: docs/proposals/02_ROUTER_RECURSION.md's 'WIRE_BUDGET is 25; 19 are spent' is correct and is not a carrier.

ITEM 5: BOTH LANDED, CONFIRMED BY READING THE TREE. K12's clause is in DEFERRED_ENTRY_POINTS['EVAL.verification_fit'] and names verify_mode; K12 PASSES. Both BYTE-IDENTICAL sentences in spine/compose.py are past-tensed with a dated note. STILL OWED, both outside my line: compose.py's 'The seven EVAL entries' against EIGHT (I checked eight commits of history -- it has been 8 in every one, so 'seven' was never right in this window, and my own document says 'eight' twice, so the two now disagree), and the CAP.d_mask_dead_rows row's `why`, whose 'Reducible' sentence I can now say is not merely ambiguous but FALSE AS WRITTEN.

ONE THING I DELIBERATELY DID NOT FIX, BECAUSE FIXING IT WOULD HAVE MEANT INVENTING A FACT: a soft cap just under the ceiling (CAP_FAB_START=4095) makes the first lift land at 4422, above the hard ceiling of 4096. Whether observe REFUSES that as at_hard_ceiling or CLAMPS it to the ceiling is a P4 decision written down nowhere, and the two answers give opposite verdicts for cap.valve. Filed as an open question rather than guessed.

NO EDGE SPENT. No wire added, no signature widened, no lever minted, no default moved, no functionality removed or stubbed. Suite green.

findings.detail:
ITEM 1, CONFIRMED AND BROADER THAN FILED. THE DEFECT: `vocab_room = vocab_armed and 0 < cv < hard_vocab` -- the honesty precondition is bound as `mask_dead` at the top of new_valve and used ONLY by the sibling gate cap.vocab_arm_honest, never by cap.valve. Since 2026-09-04 src/capacity/api.py::observe's closed block-reason set carries `dead_rows_unmasked`, which its own docstring says 'bites when the VOCABULARY arm is armed (targets in vocab|both), counters["cap.mask_dead_rows"] is False, and every other condition has passed: the lift that would have happened does not'. That is unconditional and per-flush, so on such a configuration a vocabulary lift CANNOT happen -- and cap.valve's own declared predicate is 'can a lift happen at all'. It printed FIRED. LM.mask_dead_rows defaults to False, so this is the shipped-default half of the vocabulary arm, not a corner.

WHY THE D15 CONTROL MISSED IT, MEASURED NOT ASSUMED. I drove CAP_TARGETS in (off, experts, vocab, both) x LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS in (0,1) in a fresh process each. On ALL EIGHT, cap.valve is fired=False reachable=False -- both starts are the sentinel, the sentinel resolves to the hard ceiling, and the `cap >= ceiling` arm ('no room to earn') fires before anything else can. A control run entirely inside a gate that is unreachable on every cell measures nothing, which is a property of the control and not of the change D15 made.

A FIFTH DEAD-ON-ARRIVAL, FOUND BY ME, FILED BY NOBODY, AND NEEDING NO WIRE. observe's docstring freezes the lift as derive.lift_to(cap, cap.lift, cap.lift_min), and spine/derive.py::lift_to is `int(cap) + max(int(floor), int(float(frac) * int(cap)))` -- which returns the cap UNCHANGED whenever both terms round to zero. src/capacity/levers.py::CAPLevers already records the case in as many words ('At cap 12, int(0.08 x 12) = int(0.96) = 0, so without the floor lift_to returns 12 and the cap can never move again, on any evidence, forever. That is reachable in the first place this rebuild runs -- the 200-step empty-environment CPU run with a tiny fabric'), so it is a documented, reachable configuration on which the valve was printing FIRED. It uses CAP's OWN two levers, so answering it costs no coupling and no edge.

THE REPAIR. `expert_room` and `vocab_room` each gain `_lift_moves(c)`, a nested helper that calls the SAME named derive.lift_to observe applies (a reimplementation here could disagree with the lift the valve actually takes, making the gate and the mechanism two sources of truth); `vocab_room` additionally gains `mask_dead`. The printed arithmetic gains both terms, because the file's own rule is that Gate.line prints the numbers the verdict rests on -- it now reads e.g. 'vocab 1000/ceiling 4096/one lift -> 1080/mask_dead_rows False'. The `need` string widens to match. The expert `dead` chain's bare `else` (which silently assumed 'settling point') is split into an explicit `elif ce > operating` plus a lift-size clause, and the vocabulary chain gains a mask clause and a lift-size clause, each spelled the way the existing three are. new_valve's LEVERS READ line gains `lift, lift_min` with the reason; the comment block's 'THREE WAYS AN ARMED ARM IS DEAD ON ARRIVAL' becomes FIVE and documents both new ones; the DID IT FIRE (3) line records why cap.valve reads the mask and how it differs from cap.vocab_arm_honest (precondition vs consequence, not copies). `from spine import derive` added -- legal and precedented (src/fabric/api.py, src/opt/api.py, src/tok/api.py all import it; K3/O10 refuse only assemble, registry and foreign packages).

NO COMPROMISE ANYWHERE: no signature moved, no lever minted, no default moved, no wire added, nothing removed or stubbed. The wire the mask arrives on (CAP.d_mask_dead_rows) was already declared and already delivered onto this Config, exactly as d_operating_population is, so reading it a second time costs nothing.

findings.detail:
ITEM 4, CONFIRMED, AND ITS CONSEQUENCE CLAUSE WAS FALSE TOO. Live numbers from running tests/test_couplings.py today: '23 coupling(s) resolved ...; 19 wire(s) of 25 budgeted, 4 intra-package', and `from spine.wire import WIRE_BUDGET` is 25 -- SIX edges remain. The file said 'the wire budget in spine/wire.py::WIRE_BUDGET has room for two more edges in total -- so acting on the sentence would fail at build() with an over-budget refusal'. BOTH HALVES WRONG: the count came from counting declared couplings as wires (an intra-package coupling books no edge, which is exactly the four the two numbers differ by), and the consequence falls with it -- adding the four couplings that paragraph discusses takes the ledger 19 -> 23 of the 25, which build() does not refuse.

I corrected the sentence IN PLACE (it is present tense and was live, so past-tensing alone would have left a false claim standing) and added a dated correction paragraph below it that quotes the old wording, gives the three live numbers, explains the miscount's mechanism, and records WHY IT IS NOT BOOKKEEPING: at least two agents declined to widen a signature partly because they believed the wire alternative was nearly exhausted, so a budget number wrong in the SCARCE direction silently biases every design choice that weighs a wire against an argument -- and it biases it toward the option nobody has to justify.

ONE CAUTION THE FIX HAD TO ABSORB, and it is K13 doing its job on me: my first draft wrote the hypothetical as '23 of 25' and K13 went red -- 'docs/04_CONTRACT.md:3258 says wires = 23; the tree has 19 ... A count in prose is a copy of a fact; delete it or correct it, do not add a second copy.' Correct catch: a hypothetical in the '<n> of <m> ... budget' shape is indistinguishable from a claim. Rewritten in both files as a TRANSITION ('19 -> 23 of the 25'), which is the honest form and which K13 recognises and skips. K13 now checks 57 numeric claims (up from 56 at the start of my run) and passes.

findings.detail:
THE CHECKER'S 'SECOND, SMALLER NARROWING', WHICH I AGREE WITH AND HAVE ACTED ON. The ground given for refusing per-flush rather than at startup was that a startup refusal 'would remove a configuration that runs today -- CAP_TARGETS=vocab with the shipped LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS=False'. Stated that loosely it reads as though the valve WORKS on that configuration and a startup refusal would take it away. It does not work: no vocabulary lift can happen there, this very block reason refuses every one, and after the ITEM 1 fix cap.valve reports the arm UNREACHABLE for exactly that. So the LIFTING capability is absent under both designs and is not what separates them.

THE PER-FLUSH FORM IS STILL RIGHT AND I DID NOT WEAKEN IT -- I replaced a weak ground with the real one. What separates the two designs is what the operator gets INSTEAD: a startup refusal ends the process and produces no measurement at all, while this refuses the LIFT and lets the RUN proceed -- the run trains, the expert arm still works at targets=both, the report still carries the curve, and the histogram carries a COUNT of the lifts that were earned and then declined, which is a number no other line produces and which a dead process cannot produce at all. Diagnosis over denial, on a precondition an operator fixes with one lever. The owner's decision (the stricter startup repair) is explicitly left open, as before.

WHILE THERE I RECORDED A SMALL FALSITY IN THE ROW IT CITES, which is not mine to edit: spine/assemble.py's CAP.d_mask_dead_rows row says a stricter valve 'would need no flag'. That does not hold as written -- a valve that refuses ON THIS CONDITION must still READ the condition to know when to refuse -- so the wire survives either ruling. Noted in passing in observe's docstring and filed properly under unfinished.

unfinished.title: OPEN QUESTION FOR P4, NOT A DEFECT: a soft cap just under the hard ceiling makes the FIRST lift overshoot, and nothing in the tree says whether observe refuses it or clamps it -- the two answers give cap.valve opposite verdicts
unfinished.reason: I found this while driving ITEM 1's corners and I deliberately did NOT encode an answer, because encoding one would have meant inventing a P4 behaviour that is written down nowhere. Both the code and the contract are silent, and a Gate that asserts an unfrozen behaviour is exactly the false equation this spine refuses. Filed so the person who writes observe's body decides it deliberately instead of discovering it. Nothing in my ownership line can settle it alone: it is a joint statement about capacity/api.py::observe (mine) and about what the frozen contract in docs/04_CONTRACT.md's CAP section should say (also mine) -- but it is a DESIGN decision, and taking it silently is what this item exists to prevent.
unfinished.detail:
THE CORNER. `derive.lift_to(cap, frac, floor) = int(cap) + max(int(floor), int(frac*cap))` does not clamp. At CAP_TARGETS=both CAP_FAB_START=4095 CAP_VOCAB_START=4095 LM_MASK_DEAD_ROWS=1, with hard ceilings of 4096, one lift computes 4095 + max(8, 327) = 4422 -- 326 above the ceiling. Reproduced; cap.valve prints FIRED with the arithmetic 'vocab 4095/ceiling 4096/one lift -> 4422/mask_dead_rows True'.

WHY I LEFT IT. new_valve's own comment describes at_hard_ceiling only for the cap >= ceiling case ('derive.lift_to returns cap + max(floor, frac*cap), which from a cap at or above the hard ceiling lands above it and is refused as at_hard_ceiling'). For a cap BELOW the ceiling whose lift lands above it, two readings are open and nothing distinguishes them: (i) observe REFUSES the lift as at_hard_ceiling, in which case that arm can never move and cap.valve's FIRED is another instance of exactly the ITEM 1 family; or (ii) observe CLAMPS to the hard ceiling, in which case 4095 -> 4096 is a real if tiny lift and cap.valve's FIRED is correct. CAP.observe raises NotImplementedError today, so no body settles it, and I could find no statement of it in docs/04_CONTRACT.md's CAP section, in spine/derive.py::lift_to's docstring (which documents truncation but not clamping) or in the cap_test.py known-answer table the lift replays against.

WHAT I RECOMMEND, for whoever takes it: decide it in docs/04_CONTRACT.md's CAP section and in observe's DID IT FIRE line at the same time, since the block-reason set is where the answer becomes observable. If (i), then cap.valve's `_lift_moves` helper in new_valve should become `derive.lift_to(c, cap.lift, cap.lift_min) <= hard` as well as `> c`, and the corresponding `dead` clause added -- a two-line change at the site I have already opened up for exactly this shape, needing no wire and no edge. If (ii), then the contract should SAY it clamps, because a reader of lift_to alone cannot tell. I have written neither, and the current gate is honest under (ii) and optimistic under (i) -- which is the state the question is in, and I would rather report that precisely than pick one.
